solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rush second spicy dish

parts.note: a curry is a spicy dish

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off a second time for a curry.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to move hurriedly with quick short steps, a synonym of rush.

clue.text: Royalist abroad, living alone

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters of the word before are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An exiled royalist lives a lonely life overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person or creature lives by itself, without companions.

clue.text: In the process of looting, with place being abandoned

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so the abbreviation for place drops out of the longer word

parts.note: looting is plunder, taking goods by force
PL is the usual abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: Thieves are caught mid-raid and flee the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Under means being subjected to a process, as in under construction or under review.

clue.text: Cash in study is dipped into by European

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: a thing dipped into has something put inside it, so the abbreviation for European goes inside the little word is

explanation.surface: Money set aside for studying gets raided by someone from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: READIES is British slang for ready money, cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Readies is informal British slang for banknotes or ready money.

clue.text: Uncommonly brave taking Latin oral

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the word is set out in an unusual way, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A courageous pupil takes on a Latin speaking exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' shuffles BRAVE into VERBA; 'taking' then joins on L.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal can mean spoken rather than written, the same sense as an oral agreement.

clue.text: Former winner, it's believed, maintains pressure — and that's not all

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-husband

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the word for a sure winner holds the pressure abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a cert is a horse or contender believed certain to win, a dead cert
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A one-time champion keeps up the pressure, and there is more to come.
explanation.walkthrough: CERT is British racing slang for a sure winner. The definition is cryptic: an extract is only part of a text, so it is not all.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage taken from a longer work, so it is by nature only part of the whole.

clue.text: See man in charge bagging runs

indicators.note: to bag is to pocket or capture, so the runs abbreviation is enclosed between the other two pieces

parts.note: a bishop is a man in chess, one of the pieces
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A supervisor is seen pocketing runs in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese, as in the Holy See, not the verb of looking. 'Bagging' puts the runs inside the man and the in-charge abbreviation joined.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishopric is the diocese or office of a bishop, which is also called his see.

clue.text: Secure a posh carriage

parts.note: to land a contract is to secure it
U is the British label for upper-class usage, so it stands for posh

explanation.surface: Someone acquires a fancy carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Jokes about youth leader in room in party clothes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for jokes is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a youth

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here taken from room

explanation.surface: Comedians mock a young lad in a room dressed up for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's best clothes worn for a party or occasion.

clue.text: Son winning place, in theory

parts.note: up means ahead or winning, as in two goals up
a position is a place

explanation.surface: A son wins a place, at least on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposition is a belief held without proof, the same as a theory or hypothesis.

clue.text: Endless money in old gaming house

indicators.note: a word without its end loses its last letter

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Unlimited money passes through an old-fashioned gambling den.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people gamble, a gaming house.

clue.text: Top complete/incomplete?

indicators.note: incomplete means missing a piece, here the last letter of the word for complete

parts.note: stark means complete or utter, as in stark madness

explanation.surface: A puzzling query whether the best is finished or unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash invites reading 'complete' then 'incomplete' as instructions: STARK made incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a top performer, the leading figure in a field.

clue.text: Male prison, dreadfully cold

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something done badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A men's jail is a bleak, chilly place.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersonal means lacking warmth or human feeling, which is a figurative sense of cold.

clue.text: Railway buff instructs one at the wheel?

parts.note: to train someone is to instruct them
a potter works clay at a potter's wheel

explanation.surface: A rail enthusiast teaches a driving instructor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the wheel' suggests a driver, but it is a potter's wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter is a hobbyist who logs locomotive numbers, a stereotypical railway enthusiast.

clue.text: Batting team dismissed, comprehensively

parts.note: in cricket the batting team is the side that is in, so in side
a dismissed batsman is out

explanation.surface: The batting side is bowled out completely.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in' and a dismissed batsman is 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something inside out is to know it thoroughly, so the phrase means comprehensively.

clue.text: Enter provisionally one name below writer

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces after writer sit below it, so they come after it

parts.note: a pencil is a writing instrument
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A provisional booking puts one name under an author's.
explanation.definitionFit: To pencil in an appointment is to schedule it tentatively, liable to change.

clue.text: Set about sailor after showing characteristic restraint

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word set wraps around the other pieces
after means the word for sailor follows the one for characteristic

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is described as showing his typical self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: A straitjacket is a garment that restrains the arms, a means of restraint.

clue.text: Clergyman's written about a source of nuclear energy

indicators.note: written about means placed around, so the clergyman encloses the letter a

parts.note: a rector is a clergyman; the 's is not part of the letters

explanation.surface: A vicar has written about a source of atomic power.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor is a plant where controlled fission produces energy.

clue.text: Caretaker to start to repaint after New Year's Day?

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the date

parts.note: New Year's Day is January 1st, written JAN I with Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of repaint

explanation.surface: A caretaker sets about redecorating once the new year begins.
explanation.walkthrough: JAN I is the date January 1st with I as the Roman one; TO and R follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a building's caretaker or custodian.

clue.text: Colour of satellite orbiting area close to Jupiter

indicators.note: orbiting means circling around, so the satellite word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the moon is a satellite

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of Jupiter

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes the hue of a moon circling near Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Maroon is a dark brownish-red colour.

clue.text: Legendary female reportedly produced song from 'West Side Story', nervously at first

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word for produced is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: made means produced
Maria is a famous song from the musical West Side Story

indicators.note: at first takes the first letter of nervously

explanation.surface: A legendary woman nervously performs a song from the musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Maid Marian is the sweetheart of Robin Hood in English legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid Marian is the legendary companion of Robin Hood, a female figure of folklore.

clue.text: Taken initially from large amount in bag

indicators.note: taken from means removed, so the first letter of taken comes out of the word for a large amount

parts.note: a stack, as in stacks of money, is a large amount

indicators.note: initially signals the first letter of the word taken

explanation.surface: Something removed from a big pile is put in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack is a large bag of coarse cloth.

clue.text: Guy eating a Malaysian dish

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the word for guy encloses the letter a

parts.note: a guy is a stay, a rope supporting a mast or tent

explanation.surface: A man tucks into a Malaysian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man but is a supporting rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a Southeast Asian dish of skewered grilled meat with peanut sauce.

clue.text: Closed trunk as well

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
boot is the British word for a car's trunk

explanation.surface: Someone shuts a car's luggage compartment as well.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOT is the British word for the American car trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning in addition or as well.

clue.text: Nato reorganisation unlikely, but don't mention it

indicators.note: reorganisation means rearranging, so the letters of the alliance's name are reordered

parts.note: tall means unlikely, as in a tall story

explanation.surface: A restructure of the alliance is improbable, but keep quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Not at all is a polite reply to thanks, the same idiom as don't mention it.

clue.text: Character vandalised tea urn

indicators.note: something vandalised is damaged and broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone damaged the tea urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their character or temperament.

clue.text: Original piece of cotton fabric in drawer?

indicators.note: the original piece of a word is its first letter, here of cotton

parts.note: rayon is a synthetic fabric

explanation.surface: A scrap of cotton cloth found in a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture, but here it is something one draws with.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is a stick of coloured wax used for drawing, hence a drawing implement.
